anya: Heads-up — seeing p99 spikes (~2.1s) on hosted v2 for requests with >800-token prompts, plus a few tool-calling sessions that hang. QPS steady but tail jumps.

mike: I pulled a flamegraph + kernel-selection log. For long prompts runtime flips from fused_attn to attn_chunked mid-generation which adds ~700ms on some devices.

joanna: @mike can you paste the kernel log and which model/batch sizes this was on?

mike: ```
model: llama-3-13b
seq_len: 1024 -> 2048 (prompt+prefix growth)
kernel: fused_attn64 -> attn_chunked (fallback)
microbatch: 4 -> 2 (handshake/resize)
time: gen_start 0ms; kernel_switch +680ms; kv_lookup 120ms
```

anya: repro trace saved as rdw-trace:1769001200. Long prompts often have repeated code/math blocks which seem to thrash the KV cache; also saw tool-loop sessions where a tool call spawns another tool call leading to small reentrant requests.

joanna: Could be KV cache eviction + shard boundary rehydration. What's the eviction policy? LRU per-shard?

mike: Yes LRU per-shard. When a request crosses a shard boundary we rehydrate caches which causes extra memcpy/allocs. Profiling shows memcpy spikes aligned with the kernel switch.

mike: ```
[profile] memcpy_async: 0.45s total (peaks align with kernel switch points)
[profile] gpu_alloc: 0.12s
[profile] fused_attn exec: 0.21s vs attn_chunked exec: 0.92s
[notes] KV hits drop ~30% for sequences that cross 1k->1.5k boundary
```

anya: Short-term proposal: force fused_attn for seq <= 2048 and increase microbatch handshake grace to 30ms to avoid churn. Long-term: make kernel selector KV-state-aware and detect tool-call reentrancy to avoid restarting small microbatches.

joanna: Agree. Can we A/B this on a dedicated cluster? Also add a unit/regression test for nested tool-calls that exercises KV reuse.

mike: I'll push a canary config: `kernel_override=fused_attn_max_seq=2048` and `microbatch.grace_ms=30`. Deploying to dedicated-east-2 canary now :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

sre-bot: deploy canary started by mike at 2026-03-17T14:05Z — logs: https://rwd/ops/1769001234

anya: After canary, we'll watch p95/p99, KV-cache hit rate, memcpy peaks, and tool-call success rate. I'll also assemble a small corpus of long prompts to run a synthetic sweep.

joanna: Thanks — put notes on eng-runtime board (card #498). Will mark thread closed when metrics are stable. :ok_hand:
